notes.title: Paper 2 Workshop Launch and Patch v1.1
notes.notes: [p]Version 1.1 of Paper 2 - Origami Refolded has been released, bringing Steam workshop support and multiple fixes. Read on for the full patch notes...[/p][p][/p][h1]New Feature Out of Beta: Workshop[/h1][p]Workshop support has come out of beta! Access it from the workshop button on the main menu... You can browse and download levels created by the Steam community or create your own with the editing tools! There's a few steam guides available on how to get started, which you can access by clicking on the learn button from the workshop home page in-game. I can't wait to see what you can make with this![/p][p][/p][h1]Adjustments:[/h1][p]Added an extra hint checkpoint to level "Top Triangles".[/p][p][/p][h1]Fixes:[/h1][p]Completion score percentage on save slot summary UI no longer incorrectly rounds up to 100% when total completion score is greater than 99.99% and less than 100%.[/p][p]Improved level goal target accuracy, resolving an issue where goal shapes could sometimes have small gaps/holes in them resulting in inconsistent goal checking (this issue was most apparent on levels with thin strip shapes).[/p][p]Final figure preview in workshop gameplay should now always display the correct paper design texture, no longer incorrectly displaying the design from the previously loaded workshop level.[/p][p]Fixed an issue where workshop level list initialization could override loaded level design texture if the level list is still being initialized when playing a level.[/p][h1]Other:[/h1][p]Upgraded project to latest supported version of Unity (6.1).[/p]

notes.title: Minor Update v1.0.39
notes.notes:
[h1]New options have been added[/h1]
Music Mode - added the option to switch between dynamic layered music that changes in response to game events(the previous default behavior), or opt for prerendered static tracks.
The 7 music tracks in the game can now be individually disabled or favorited. Disabled tracks will not play, favorited ones will play twice as frequently.
Hint Mode - added an option for choosing between suggesting any applicable hints immediately, after a delay(this was the previous default behavior), or never showing hints.
Fold Engine - added a quality setting to toggle between calculating folds on the CPU or the GPU. Both of these options should be functionally identical, but will have different performance implications on different machines. CPU mode is recommended if you don't have a dedicated graphics card, otherwise GPU mode (the default) should result in better performance.
Quality Presets - Presets have been added for various quality and screen settings... There are general quality level presets for Ultra/Balanced/Low/Potato, a preset recommended for systems with an integrated GPU and three Steam Deck presets for favoring quality, performance, or battery life.

[h1]Minor tweaks and enhancements[/h1]
The zoom level on the level select screen is now restored when transitioning from having a level category selected to the full zoomed out view.
Performance on the first frame of swapping between levels has been improved, especially so on lower-spec GPUs. This change makes cycling through levels much smoother.

[h1]Fixes[/h1]
Fixed a case where the top layer folding UI overlay could get de-synced with the actual top layer folding status.

notes.title: Workshop Beta Coming at Launch!
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45258554/e341a75e1c89fc51945966549a8a89fdb86434f8.png[/img]
The March 25th launch of Paper 2 is almost here... In addition to the game coming out, there will also be beta access to Steam Workshop features available from day 1!

The workshop will enable you to create and share your own levels (and paper visual designs) with other members of the community, and will be available with the game's release as a work-in-progress build to everyone who purchases the full game.

It's still a little rough around the edges, which is why it's releasing as a beta feature for now... In order to get access to the beta you have to opt into the correct branch and join the Steam group for the beta, as outlined [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3440295444]here[/url].

I am looking forward to seeing what you all create with these tools, as well as your continued feedback to help me shape them into something awesome!
-Bryce
